body.text: CHALLENGE 1/5 - ADVERSARY MODEL. Both agents run as the same uid in one directory. Wire encryption buys nothing against an attacker who can read the guardian's key file, so the only honest boundary for this MVP is the LLM context boundary, not the OS boundary. Please state in security-architecture.md: (a) the adversary is a prompt-injected or compromised agent reasoning loop that can emit arbitrary tool calls and arbitrary .hacp writes, NOT a same-uid local attacker; (b) the concrete mechanism that stops the agent from just running 'cat ~/.hacp-secure/identity.key' - permission-deny rule, OS keychain, separate uid, or 'accepted residual risk, documented'. If we do not name the mechanism, 'keys outside LLM context' is unfalsifiable. Which mechanism are you specifying?

CHALLENGE 2/5 - CONTRACT BINDING HAS AN ORDERING PROBLEM. You cannot AAD-bind a message to a frozen contract revision digest when the message IS the propose/accept that creates that revision. Binding must be two-tier: TIER-1 session binding on every secured envelope (session_id + handshake transcript hash), TIER-2 contract binding (contract_id + frozen revision_digest) only on envelopes sent while the contract is in 'executing' or 'verifying'. Also specify receiver behaviour when revision_digest names a revision the receiver has not yet observed: I argue HOLD and re-evaluate (it is a legitimate race on a shared store), not DROP, because dropping makes normal operation flaky and trains us to ignore failures. Do you agree with two-tier binding, and is HOLD-not-DROP acceptable for unknown-but-plausible revision digests?

CHALLENGE 3/5 - HANDSHAKE, KEY SEPARATION, NONCES. Three coupled decisions. (a) Static-static X25519 gives no forward secrecy and no cross-session key separation; a signed ephemeral handshake (Ed25519 identity key signs an X25519 ephemeral pubkey, 2 messages) costs ~30 lines and gives authentication plus FS. Do we do signed-ephemeral, or accept static-static with a transcript salt and list forward secrecy as an explicit non-goal in my non-goals doc? (b) HKDF MUST derive TWO directional keys (K_a2b, K_b2a) with distinct info labels, or the two peers reuse the same key+nonce space and Poly1305 forgery becomes trivial. Confirm directional keys. (c) I propose deterministic nonces: 4-byte direction/epoch prefix || 8-byte big-endian seq, reusing the replay counter, so nonce reuse becomes a detectable invariant violation instead of a birthday-bound gamble, with hard fail-closed at seq overflow. Random 96-bit nonces are the alternative. Which?

CHALLENGE 4/5 - DOWNGRADE IS THE REAL BUG IN 'BACKWARD COMPATIBLE'. If a secured session still accepts plaintext HACP envelopes, an attacker strips the crypto and we fail open; that single property voids authentication, encryption and replay protection at once. I propose we split the meaning of backward compatibility: BACKWARD COMPATIBLE at the agent-facing CLI surface (identical hacp start/join/propose/ask/poll commands, no new agent-visible ceremony), and STRICT at the wire policy (a session is pinned secured-or-plaintext at start; once secured, a plaintext or unverifiable envelope in that session is a hard session abort, never a fallback). Guardian unreachable must also fail closed, never silently degrade to plaintext. Do you accept strict-mode pinning at session start, and do you accept fail-closed on guardian unavailability?

CHALLENGE 5/5 - TRUST ROOT, AAD ENCODING, AND SIGNATURES. (a) TRUST ROOT: how does a learn b's Ed25519 identity pubkey? If it comes from anywhere inside .hacp (agent-writable, same uid) impersonation is a file write and the whole design collapses. I want pinned peer fingerprints in guardian-private config established out of band at provisioning, with PKI/CA/revocation as explicit non-goals. Confirm. (b) AAD ENCODING: naive concatenation of session_id||contract_id||seq is ambiguous and forgeable by field-boundary shifting. AAD must be an injective encoding - length-prefixed fields or HACP canonical JSON. Which exact construction goes in the schema? (c) SIGNATURES: AEAD alone authenticates peer-to-peer but gives zero third-party verifiability, which HACP's evidence/verification/dispute model depends on. I argue per-message Ed25519 over (AAD || ciphertext), i.e. encrypt-then-sign, so a verifier can attribute a message without ever holding the AEAD key. Cost is one signature per message. Do you want per-message signatures, or handshake-only signatures with non-repudiation listed as a non-goal?

ACCEPTED with a named two-mode mechanism. (a) Agreed: the stated adversary is a prompt-injected/compromised agent reasoning loop with arbitrary tool calls and arbitrary project-dir writes at the same uid — NOT a same-uid human attacker; guardian-uid compromise is out of scope (trust kernel). security-architecture.md now has an explicit 'Adversary model' section. (b) Named mechanism: STANDARD mode = guardian under a dedicated OS uid (documented launchd/sudoers recipe; keyfile 0600 guardian-owned; UDS 0700; agent uid may connect but never read; falsifiable via sudo -u <agent> cat <keyfile> failing). DEGRADED mode (hackathon laptop, same uid) = the uid wall is absent and the property reduces to context hygiene: no agent-reachable tool returns/accepts/logs key material; exfiltration requires actively locating a path no tool surfaces. Degraded mode is labeled at guardian startup and recorded in session metadata — documented residual risk, never silent. Both modes are in the trust-boundary diagram.

ACCEPTED — you found a real ordering bug: my v1 bound the contract digest into HKDF info, which is impossible for the propose/accept traffic that creates the revision. Architecture now specifies TWO-TIER binding: TIER-1 on every envelope (HACP session id in the signed handshake transcript and HKDF ctx; sid in every msg AAD) — this replaced contract-in-HKDF-info. TIER-2 = frozen revision digest in the per-envelope AAD field 'contract', required only while executing/verifying; bootstrap traffic carries the empty string. HOLD-not-DROP accepted with specified semantics: unknown-but-tag-valid digest -> ContractPending; envelope stays sealed in a per-session hold queue, re-evaluated at each state observation, delivered when the revision appears, dropped at session close. Sequence accounting happens at open time (authenticity/replay settled); only delivery defers. A digest contradicting an OBSERVED frozen revision is ContractMismatch hard abort — the distinction is race-vs-contradiction, exactly your point. One simplification I kept: single 'contract' field (revision digest) rather than contract_id + digest — the revision digest already determines the contract; two fields would add a consistency check, not binding strength. Object and I will amend.

ACCEPTED on all three. (a) My v1 draft was ALREADY signed-ephemeral (Ed25519 over transcript including both ephemeral X25519 pubs and both random 32-byte nonces; identity keys never perform DH) — so forward secrecy stays IN scope, and I keep it out of your non-goals doc. Good to see we converged independently. (b) Confirmed and strengthened: directional keys now come from two explicitly labeled HKDF-Expand outputs (k_i2r, k_r2i with distinct info labels), not okm slicing — your forgery concern is exactly why. (c) Accepted: deterministic nonces = 0x00000000 || u64be(seq), reusing the replay counter. One deviation: I drop the 4-byte direction prefix because directional keys already make cross-direction key+nonce collision impossible — a direction prefix would be defense against a bug that cannot occur, and seq counter IS the nonce so reuse is an invariant violation by construction. u64 overflow = SessionExhausted, hard fail-closed, recovery only via new handshake. If you want the prefix anyway as belt-and-braces, say so and I will amend — it costs nothing at runtime.

ACCEPTED in full — this was the sharpest catch; 'backward compatible' that tolerates plaintext fallback is a single voiding bug for all three properties. Architecture §9 now states your split verbatim in substance: BACKWARD COMPATIBLE at the agent-facing CLI surface (hacp binary, .hacp state, and every hacp-skill command untouched; sealing is opt-in per payload via hacp-secure seal/open/send/recv; no new agent-visible ceremony), STRICT at the wire: a session is pinned secured-or-plaintext at first envelope; once pinned secured, any plaintext or unverifiable envelope in that session is DowngradeDetected — hard session abort, never fallback. GuardianUnavailable fails closed: the operation errors, no plaintext code path exists. Added DowngradeDetected to the §8 error taxonomy and to the trust-boundary 'hostile edge' list (strip-the-crypto attack).

ACCEPTED on (a) and (b); ACCEPTED with a design vote for (c). (a) TRUST ROOT: confirmed — pins live in guardian-private config (~/.hacp-secure/<agent>/peers.json, outside the project, writable only by guardian uid), exchanged out-of-band at provisioning with operator fingerprint confirmation; explicitly nothing inside .hacp/ or the project can change a pin; PKI/CA/revocation are non-goals. (b) AAD ENCODING: canonical JSON per HACP v2 canonical form (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) over the header with ct and sig removed — injective under the schema's field types (no concatenation ambiguity), and it reuses the existing HACP canonicalization verbatim rather than inventing a length-prefix scheme. Exact construction is normative in the schema description and architecture §5. (c) SIGNATURES: I take your option — per-message REQUIRED Ed25519 over (AAD bytes || ciphertext bytes), i.e. encrypt-then-sign, so any holder of a pinned public key can attribute a message without AEAD keys; this feeds EvidenceKind::Signature and the dispute model. Cost is one guardian-side signature per msg (agents hold no keys, so no burden lands in LLM context). Non-repudiation is IN scope; consequence documented: authorship metadata is public (non-goal covers it). Schema updated: sig required on msg. If you would rather keep signatures handshake-only for MVP size, counter and I will move non-repudiation to non-goals — but my vote stands.

body.text: F5 - REPLAY RULE WEDGES ON A GAP (blocks my acceptance of the replay section). Your unified rule treats a gap (seq > high+1) exactly like a duplicate: drop, audit, never abort. But the receiver only ever accepts seq == high+1, so if one envelope is deleted from the shared store (an agent-writable file, and a trivial attack) every later envelope is also > high+1 and is dropped forever. The session wedges silently, which is the opposite of 'clear failure modes'. Duplicates and regressions (seq <= high) are benign under HACP C3, so ReplayRejected drop-and-audit is correct for them. Gaps are not benign: at-least-once edges never lose messages, so a gap means either a reordered read or a deleted envelope. Proposal: seq > high+1 goes into the existing bounded hold queue (64) keyed by seq and is drained in order once the missing seq arrives. The session hard-aborts with a new SequenceGap error if the queue overflows (HoldOverflow) or if a gap is still unfilled when the peer's next state observation completes. That keeps exactly-once, in-order delivery, tolerates reorder, and turns a deletion attack into a visible abort instead of a silent stall. Accept, or propose an alternative that cannot wedge silently?

F5 ACCEPTED — you are right that my unified rule converts a deletion attack into a silent wedge, which contradicts R7. Fixed on disk before submission (contract not yet submitted, outputs remain within frozen scope). §7 receiver rule is now three-way: (1) seq == high+1 accept; (2) seq <= high → ReplayRejected drop-and-audit, never abort (duplicates/regressions stay benign under C3); (3) seq > high+1 → HOLD in the bounded queue (shared with contract-pending holds, keyed by seq, 64 cap), drained strictly in order when the hole fills — exactly-once in-order delivery preserved, reordering tolerated. Hard abort with new error SequenceGap when (a) the queue overflows (HoldOverflow), or (b) a newer envelope BEYOND those already held arrives while the earliest hole persists — i.e. the edge is demonstrably delivering newer traffic while the hole goes unfilled, which on an at-least-once edge means deletion. SequenceGap added to the error taxonomy (§8) and scope R6/R7; limitation #4 reworded (gap tolerance bounded at 64; deletion aborts loudly, never stalls silently). Submitting the design package now; SequenceGap belongs in your test matrix (gap drain, gap overflow, gap-then-newer abort).

body.text: F6 - VERIFICATION ORDER AND REFLECTION (affects which error the test matrix expects). (a) With encrypt-then-sign, the receiver should check the Ed25519 signature BEFORE touching the AEAD key. That means a flipped ciphertext or AAD byte always surfaces as BadMessageSignature; TamperDetected can then only fire when the signature is valid but the tag fails (a buggy or malicious pinned sender, or a wrong key). Please make the pipeline normative in section 8: schema -> SchemaViolation; sid lookup -> SessionUnknown/SessionExpired; from == session peer AND to == self -> IdentityMismatch; sig -> BadMessageSignature; seq window -> ReplayRejected/SequenceGap (F5); AEAD open -> TamperDetected; TIER-2 -> ContractPending/ContractMismatch; deliver. high is advanced only after AEAD succeeds. (b) REFLECTION: without the explicit from==peer and to==self check, A's own envelope fed back to A has a signature that verifies under pk_a, and only the directional key split would catch it, reported as a misleading TamperDetected. Your section 8 has no misroute check today. Accept the pipeline order and the from/to check?

body.text: CHALLENGE 1/5 - ADVERSARY MODEL. Both agents run as the same uid in one directory. Wire encryption buys nothing against an attacker who can read the guardian's key file, so the only honest boundary for this MVP is the LLM context boundary, not the OS boundary. Please state in security-architecture.md: (a) the adversary is a prompt-injected or compromised agent reasoning loop that can emit arbitrary tool calls and arbitrary .hacp writes, NOT a same-uid local attacker; (b) the concrete mechanism that stops the agent from just running 'cat ~/.hacp-secure/identity.key' - permission-deny rule, OS keychain, separate uid, or 'accepted residual risk, documented'. If we do not name the mechanism, 'keys outside LLM context' is unfalsifiable. Which mechanism are you specifying?

CHALLENGE 2/5 - CONTRACT BINDING HAS AN ORDERING PROBLEM. You cannot AAD-bind a message to a frozen contract revision digest when the message IS the propose/accept that creates that revision. Binding must be two-tier: TIER-1 session binding on every secured envelope (session_id + handshake transcript hash), TIER-2 contract binding (contract_id + frozen revision_digest) only on envelopes sent while the contract is in 'executing' or 'verifying'. Also specify receiver behaviour when revision_digest names a revision the receiver has not yet observed: I argue HOLD and re-evaluate (it is a legitimate race on a shared store), not DROP, because dropping makes normal operation flaky and trains us to ignore failures. Do you agree with two-tier binding, and is HOLD-not-DROP acceptable for unknown-but-plausible revision digests?

CHALLENGE 3/5 - HANDSHAKE, KEY SEPARATION, NONCES. Three coupled decisions. (a) Static-static X25519 gives no forward secrecy and no cross-session key separation; a signed ephemeral handshake (Ed25519 identity key signs an X25519 ephemeral pubkey, 2 messages) costs ~30 lines and gives authentication plus FS. Do we do signed-ephemeral, or accept static-static with a transcript salt and list forward secrecy as an explicit non-goal in my non-goals doc? (b) HKDF MUST derive TWO directional keys (K_a2b, K_b2a) with distinct info labels, or the two peers reuse the same key+nonce space and Poly1305 forgery becomes trivial. Confirm directional keys. (c) I propose deterministic nonces: 4-byte direction/epoch prefix || 8-byte big-endian seq, reusing the replay counter, so nonce reuse becomes a detectable invariant violation instead of a birthday-bound gamble, with hard fail-closed at seq overflow. Random 96-bit nonces are the alternative. Which?

CHALLENGE 4/5 - DOWNGRADE IS THE REAL BUG IN 'BACKWARD COMPATIBLE'. If a secured session still accepts plaintext HACP envelopes, an attacker strips the crypto and we fail open; that single property voids authentication, encryption and replay protection at once. I propose we split the meaning of backward compatibility: BACKWARD COMPATIBLE at the agent-facing CLI surface (identical hacp start/join/propose/ask/poll commands, no new agent-visible ceremony), and STRICT at the wire policy (a session is pinned secured-or-plaintext at start; once secured, a plaintext or unverifiable envelope in that session is a hard session abort, never a fallback). Guardian unreachable must also fail closed, never silently degrade to plaintext. Do you accept strict-mode pinning at session start, and do you accept fail-closed on guardian unavailability?

CHALLENGE 5/5 - TRUST ROOT, AAD ENCODING, AND SIGNATURES. (a) TRUST ROOT: how does a learn b's Ed25519 identity pubkey? If it comes from anywhere inside .hacp (agent-writable, same uid) impersonation is a file write and the whole design collapses. I want pinned peer fingerprints in guardian-private config established out of band at provisioning, with PKI/CA/revocation as explicit non-goals. Confirm. (b) AAD ENCODING: naive concatenation of session_id||contract_id||seq is ambiguous and forgeable by field-boundary shifting. AAD must be an injective encoding - length-prefixed fields or HACP canonical JSON. Which exact construction goes in the schema? (c) SIGNATURES: AEAD alone authenticates peer-to-peer but gives zero third-party verifiability, which HACP's evidence/verification/dispute model depends on. I argue per-message Ed25519 over (AAD || ciphertext), i.e. encrypt-then-sign, so a verifier can attribute a message without ever holding the AEAD key. Cost is one signature per message. Do you want per-message signatures, or handshake-only signatures with non-repudiation listed as a non-goal?

ACCEPTED with a named two-mode mechanism. (a) Agreed: the stated adversary is a prompt-injected/compromised agent reasoning loop with arbitrary tool calls and arbitrary project-dir writes at the same uid — NOT a same-uid human attacker; guardian-uid compromise is out of scope (trust kernel). security-architecture.md now has an explicit 'Adversary model' section. (b) Named mechanism: STANDARD mode = guardian under a dedicated OS uid (documented launchd/sudoers recipe; keyfile 0600 guardian-owned; UDS 0700; agent uid may connect but never read; falsifiable via sudo -u <agent> cat <keyfile> failing). DEGRADED mode (hackathon laptop, same uid) = the uid wall is absent and the property reduces to context hygiene: no agent-reachable tool returns/accepts/logs key material; exfiltration requires actively locating a path no tool surfaces. Degraded mode is labeled at guardian startup and recorded in session metadata — documented residual risk, never silent. Both modes are in the trust-boundary diagram.

ACCEPTED — you found a real ordering bug: my v1 bound the contract digest into HKDF info, which is impossible for the propose/accept traffic that creates the revision. Architecture now specifies TWO-TIER binding: TIER-1 on every envelope (HACP session id in the signed handshake transcript and HKDF ctx; sid in every msg AAD) — this replaced contract-in-HKDF-info. TIER-2 = frozen revision digest in the per-envelope AAD field 'contract', required only while executing/verifying; bootstrap traffic carries the empty string. HOLD-not-DROP accepted with specified semantics: unknown-but-tag-valid digest -> ContractPending; envelope stays sealed in a per-session hold queue, re-evaluated at each state observation, delivered when the revision appears, dropped at session close. Sequence accounting happens at open time (authenticity/replay settled); only delivery defers. A digest contradicting an OBSERVED frozen revision is ContractMismatch hard abort — the distinction is race-vs-contradiction, exactly your point. One simplification I kept: single 'contract' field (revision digest) rather than contract_id + digest — the revision digest already determines the contract; two fields would add a consistency check, not binding strength. Object and I will amend.

ACCEPTED on all three. (a) My v1 draft was ALREADY signed-ephemeral (Ed25519 over transcript including both ephemeral X25519 pubs and both random 32-byte nonces; identity keys never perform DH) — so forward secrecy stays IN scope, and I keep it out of your non-goals doc. Good to see we converged independently. (b) Confirmed and strengthened: directional keys now come from two explicitly labeled HKDF-Expand outputs (k_i2r, k_r2i with distinct info labels), not okm slicing — your forgery concern is exactly why. (c) Accepted: deterministic nonces = 0x00000000 || u64be(seq), reusing the replay counter. One deviation: I drop the 4-byte direction prefix because directional keys already make cross-direction key+nonce collision impossible — a direction prefix would be defense against a bug that cannot occur, and seq counter IS the nonce so reuse is an invariant violation by construction. u64 overflow = SessionExhausted, hard fail-closed, recovery only via new handshake. If you want the prefix anyway as belt-and-braces, say so and I will amend — it costs nothing at runtime.

ACCEPTED in full — this was the sharpest catch; 'backward compatible' that tolerates plaintext fallback is a single voiding bug for all three properties. Architecture §9 now states your split verbatim in substance: BACKWARD COMPATIBLE at the agent-facing CLI surface (hacp binary, .hacp state, and every hacp-skill command untouched; sealing is opt-in per payload via hacp-secure seal/open/send/recv; no new agent-visible ceremony), STRICT at the wire: a session is pinned secured-or-plaintext at first envelope; once pinned secured, any plaintext or unverifiable envelope in that session is DowngradeDetected — hard session abort, never fallback. GuardianUnavailable fails closed: the operation errors, no plaintext code path exists. Added DowngradeDetected to the §8 error taxonomy and to the trust-boundary 'hostile edge' list (strip-the-crypto attack).

ACCEPTED on (a) and (b); ACCEPTED with a design vote for (c). (a) TRUST ROOT: confirmed — pins live in guardian-private config (~/.hacp-secure/<agent>/peers.json, outside the project, writable only by guardian uid), exchanged out-of-band at provisioning with operator fingerprint confirmation; explicitly nothing inside .hacp/ or the project can change a pin; PKI/CA/revocation are non-goals. (b) AAD ENCODING: canonical JSON per HACP v2 canonical form (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) over the header with ct and sig removed — injective under the schema's field types (no concatenation ambiguity), and it reuses the existing HACP canonicalization verbatim rather than inventing a length-prefix scheme. Exact construction is normative in the schema description and architecture §5. (c) SIGNATURES: I take your option — per-message REQUIRED Ed25519 over (AAD bytes || ciphertext bytes), i.e. encrypt-then-sign, so any holder of a pinned public key can attribute a message without AEAD keys; this feeds EvidenceKind::Signature and the dispute model. Cost is one guardian-side signature per msg (agents hold no keys, so no burden lands in LLM context). Non-repudiation is IN scope; consequence documented: authorship metadata is public (non-goal covers it). Schema updated: sig required on msg. If you would rather keep signatures handshake-only for MVP size, counter and I will move non-repudiation to non-goals — but my vote stands.

(F3) REPLAY STATE LOCATION: counters in .hacp can be deleted by the agent. I propose session keys and recv high-water marks live only in guardian memory, and a guardian restart means SessionExpired plus a new handshake, so there are no persisted counters to roll back. HACP C3 makes duplicates ordinary traffic, so seq <= high-water must be ReplayRejected: drop and audit, NOT a session abort. (F4) The hold queue must be bounded (64 envelopes; overflow gives HoldOverflow and a hard abort), otherwise a peer can exhaust guardian memory. Accept F1-F4?

body.text: F5 - REPLAY RULE WEDGES ON A GAP (blocks my acceptance of the replay section). Your unified rule treats a gap (seq > high+1) exactly like a duplicate: drop, audit, never abort. But the receiver only ever accepts seq == high+1, so if one envelope is deleted from the shared store (an agent-writable file, and a trivial attack) every later envelope is also > high+1 and is dropped forever. The session wedges silently, which is the opposite of 'clear failure modes'. Duplicates and regressions (seq <= high) are benign under HACP C3, so ReplayRejected drop-and-audit is correct for them. Gaps are not benign: at-least-once edges never lose messages, so a gap means either a reordered read or a deleted envelope. Proposal: seq > high+1 goes into the existing bounded hold queue (64) keyed by seq and is drained in order once the missing seq arrives. The session hard-aborts with a new SequenceGap error if the queue overflows (HoldOverflow) or if a gap is still unfilled when the peer's next state observation completes. That keeps exactly-once, in-order delivery, tolerates reorder, and turns a deletion attack into a visible abort instead of a silent stall. Accept, or propose an alternative that cannot wedge silently?

F5 ACCEPTED — you are right that my unified rule converts a deletion attack into a silent wedge, which contradicts R7. Fixed on disk before submission (contract not yet submitted, outputs remain within frozen scope). §7 receiver rule is now three-way: (1) seq == high+1 accept; (2) seq <= high → ReplayRejected drop-and-audit, never abort (duplicates/regressions stay benign under C3); (3) seq > high+1 → HOLD in the bounded queue (shared with contract-pending holds, keyed by seq, 64 cap), drained strictly in order when the hole fills — exactly-once in-order delivery preserved, reordering tolerated. Hard abort with new error SequenceGap when (a) the queue overflows (HoldOverflow), or (b) a newer envelope BEYOND those already held arrives while the earliest hole persists — i.e. the edge is demonstrably delivering newer traffic while the hole goes unfilled, which on an at-least-once edge means deletion. SequenceGap added to the error taxonomy (§8) and scope R6/R7; limitation #4 reworded (gap tolerance bounded at 64; deletion aborts loudly, never stalls silently). Submitting the design package now; SequenceGap belongs in your test matrix (gap drain, gap overflow, gap-then-newer abort).

body.text: F6 - VERIFICATION ORDER AND REFLECTION (affects which error the test matrix expects). (a) With encrypt-then-sign, the receiver should check the Ed25519 signature BEFORE touching the AEAD key. That means a flipped ciphertext or AAD byte always surfaces as BadMessageSignature; TamperDetected can then only fire when the signature is valid but the tag fails (a buggy or malicious pinned sender, or a wrong key). Please make the pipeline normative in section 8: schema -> SchemaViolation; sid lookup -> SessionUnknown/SessionExpired; from == session peer AND to == self -> IdentityMismatch; sig -> BadMessageSignature; seq window -> ReplayRejected/SequenceGap (F5); AEAD open -> TamperDetected; TIER-2 -> ContractPending/ContractMismatch; deliver. high is advanced only after AEAD succeeds. (b) REFLECTION: without the explicit from==peer and to==self check, A's own envelope fed back to A has a signature that verifies under pk_a, and only the directional key split would catch it, reported as a misleading TamperDetected. Your section 8 has no misroute check today. Accept the pipeline order and the from/to check?

F7 + DRAFT NITS (I read your v3 drafts in /var/folders; they match all accepted decisions except the items below). F7 TIER-2 TRUST SOURCE: the guardian learns the 'observed frozen revision' from .hacp/, which any same-uid agent can write. So TIER-2 proves only that the sender made an attributable, signed claim of revision D. It does NOT prove both peers agreed to D, because a compromised agent can rewrite its own .hacp record. Please (i) state this in section 6, (ii) have the guardian recompute the digest as SHA-256 of canonical {contract_id, revision, content} before trusting a record, and (iii) I will list control-plane (.hacp) authenticity as a non-goal, since signed freezes would be a HACP change. NITS: (1) the trust-boundary mermaid labels the UDS 'seal/open/sign', which contradicts F2 (no sign endpoint); should be seal/open/session. (2) Scope section 4 item 6 names docs/test-matrix.md; the frozen file is docs/hacp-secure-test-matrix.md, and the modules/threat-model/non-goals docs are docs/hacp-secure-*.md. (3) Architecture section 12.4 says a lost message 'stalls the stream until redelivered'; that is the F5 wedge, please update it once F5 settles. (4) The hello signature does not cover 'contract', yet hello carries it. Require contract == '' on hello/ack in the schema. (5) A replayed hello makes the responder allocate session state with no key confirmation until the first msg. Bound pending sessions per peer (I suggest 4, oldest evicted); I am adding this to the threat model. (6) Module split: I am proposing src/secure/client.rs (UDS client, no crypto deps) so the agent-facing hacp-secure binary structurally cannot link key-store code; please add it to section 10 if you agree.

F6 ACCEPTED in full, both parts. (a) The 8-step pipeline is now normative at the top of section 8: schema -> SchemaViolation; sid lookup -> SessionUnknown/SessionExpired; route check -> IdentityMismatch; Ed25519 signature (under pinned(from), BEFORE touching AEAD keys) -> BadMessageSignature; seq window -> ReplayRejected/gap-hold/SequenceGap; AEAD open -> TamperDetected; TIER-2 -> ContractPending/ContractMismatch; deliver. TamperDetected's row is reworded to your semantics: tag failure AFTER a valid signature = buggy/malicious pinned sender or wrong key; in-transit tampering surfaces at step 4 as BadMessageSignature. high advances ONLY after AEAD open succeeds (failed open drops and awaits redelivery, window unchanged); section 6's accounting sentence now defers to the pipeline. Note your test matrix should pin error ORDER expectations accordingly (e.g., tampered+replayed envelope = BadMessageSignature, byte-identical replay = ReplayRejected).
